content.user_title: Design Better REST and GraphQL APIs
content.value_statement: API teams need consistent contracts before implementation starts. This skill guides resource design, request formats, errors, versioning, and documentation.
actual_capabilities: Guides REST resource naming, HTTP methods, and status code selection.
Defines request, response, and error formats for API contracts.
Covers pagination, filtering, sorting, field selection, and batch operation patterns.
Compares authentication options and common API versioning approaches.
Provides OpenAPI 3.0 structure for documenting endpoints and schemas.
Shows when GraphQL may fit better than REST for related data.
limitations: Does not execute API servers, migrations, tests, or deployment commands.
Uses generic examples that must be adapted to the product domain.
Does not replace threat modeling or framework-specific security review.
Does not verify live API behavior or production documentation accuracy.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Service API
use_cases.description: Define resources, endpoints, status codes, and response shapes before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Review an Existing API Contract
use_cases.description: Find naming, pagination, error, and versioning inconsistencies in a current API design.

use_cases.title: Prepare Developer Documentation
use_cases.description: Turn endpoint requirements into clear OpenAPI-oriented documentation and integration examples.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic REST Endpoints
prompt_templates.prompt: Design REST endpoints for a {resource} resource. Include methods, paths, status codes, and simple request and response descriptions.

prompt_templates.title: Add Pagination and Filtering
prompt_templates.prompt: Design list endpoints for {resource}. Include pagination, filtering, sorting, field selection, and example error cases.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an OpenAPI Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an OpenAPI-oriented outline for {service}. Include endpoints, schemas, authentication, errors, and versioning guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Compare REST and GraphQL
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate REST and GraphQL designs for {domain}. Recommend one approach and explain tradeoffs for data shape, caching, auth, and versioning.

output_examples.input: Design a user management API for account profiles and roles.
output: A resource map for users, roles, and memberships.
Endpoint descriptions with methods, status codes, and validation notes.
A consistent error response model and pagination strategy.

output_examples.input: Review a product catalog API before frontend integration.
output: A checklist of naming, filtering, sorting, and caching issues.
Recommended endpoint changes with compatibility notes.
Documentation gaps that may block frontend or partner teams.

output_examples.input: Decide whether an analytics dashboard should use REST or GraphQL.
output: A comparison of query flexibility, caching, schema evolution, and client complexity.
A recommended architecture with risks and migration considerations.

best_practices: Start with clear resources, relationships, and authorization rules before naming endpoints.
Keep response, error, pagination, and versioning patterns consistent across services.
Document schemas and examples alongside endpoint decisions so contracts stay reviewable.
anti_patterns: Mixing verbs and nouns in paths without a consistent resource model.
Adding custom error shapes for each endpoint without shared codes and fields.
Choosing GraphQL only to hide unclear resource boundaries or authorization rules.

faq.question: Does this skill generate production API code?
faq.answer: No. It guides API design and documentation, but implementation remains project-specific.

faq.question: Can it help with OpenAPI documents?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines OpenAPI 3.0 structures, schemas, paths, responses, and authentication sections.

faq.question: Does it support GraphQL design?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes GraphQL schema guidance and helps compare GraphQL with REST.

faq.question: Can it review existing endpoints?
faq.answer: Yes. It can assess naming, consistency, pagination, errors, authentication, and versioning choices.

faq.question: Does it make live network calls?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation guidance and does not call external APIs.
